message:
feat(update): one address is enough -- the manifest url comes from the directory

The update manifest url only ever came from an environment variable on
Windows and a build constant on Android. The server has had a
/api/update/manifest route the whole time. So a machine configured with a
server address and nothing else could never check for updates: the address
was there, the route was there, and nothing joined them.

It is derived from the directory origin now, and an explicit override still
wins, so a deployment that set the variable is not moved onto a different
server by this.

Built from the origin rather than by pasting strings -- directory_origin_key
and originKey decide scheme, host and port -- so a trailing slash, a path or
a written-out default port cannot end up in the middle of the url. The
signature is not fetched separately: the server puts the document and its
detached signature in one response.

An http directory derives nothing. Guessing https invents a server nobody
configured; following the directory down to http fetches something that will
run with administrator rights over a hop anyone can rewrite. Such a
deployment says where its updates are with an explicit https override, and
until it does the answer is "not configured" rather than a failure.

Fixing this exposed one on Android: after fetching the document it asked for
"$manifestUrl.sig", which the server has never served -- appending .sig to
/api/update/manifest?platform=android lands inside a query value. Nobody had
noticed because the url was an empty build constant, so the line had never
run. Deriving the url makes it reachable, so it now reads both fields out of
the one response, the way the Windows client does. The https-only guard
above it is untouched.

NOT fixed, and it blocks the feature from actually working: that route
requires a session or an x-host-token, and neither client's fetcher sends
one, so a derived url gets 401 today. Threading a token into the update
fetch is a decision about which credential goes to which origin, and it is
not one to make quietly on the way past.
